title: Blueprint node hom-pfr: homomorphism form of PFR glued from goursat and pfr-9-aux'
intent: Freeze the statement and Lean name of the chapter headline node `hom-pfr` (`homomorphism_pfr`) before its proof, then prove it with a covering-and-counting argument over the graph of `f` that composes exactly two already-stated nodes — `goursat`, which factorises a subspace of `G × G'`, and `pfr-9-aux'`, which covers a set by a subgroup `H` — so the proof is a short glue between two named lemma holes.

parent.name: hom-pfr
parent.statement: Let f : G → G' be a function and S := { f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y) : x,y ∈ G }. Then there exists a homomorphism φ : G → G' such that |{ f(x)-φ(x) : x ∈ G }| ≤ |S|^{10} (Lean name homomorphism_pfr).

children.name: goursat
children.statement: Let H be a subgroup of G × G'. Then there exist a subgroup H₀ of G, a subgroup H₁ of G', and a homomorphism φ : G → G' such that H = { (x, φ(x)+y) : x ∈ H₀, y ∈ H₁ }; in particular |H| = |H₀| |H₁| (Lean name goursat).
children.closed_by: its own proof (hom_pfr.tex:16-17) cites \Cref{hb-thm}, the Hahn-Banach extension lemma proved by induction in the same file, and closes the size bound by direct counting; in Lean, goursat (PFR/HomPFR.lean:46-65) closes by obtain/use/constructor

children.name: pfr-9-aux'
children.statement: If |A+A| ≤ K|A|, then there exist a subgroup H and a subset c of G with A ⊆ c+H, such that |c| ≤ K^5 |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2} and |H|/|A| ∈ [K^{-8}, K^8] (Lean name better_PFR_conjecture_aux).
children.closed_by: its own proof (further_improvement.tex:369-373) applies \Cref{pfr-9-aux} and \Cref{ruz-cov}; in Lean, better_PFR_conjecture_aux (PFR/RhoFunctional.lean:2003-2043) closes from better_PFR_conjecture_aux0 and Set.ruzsa_covering_add

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem whose conclusion witnesses an object (a homomorphism φ close to an approximate homomorphism f), proved as a short calculation that combines two named lemmas: an algebraic structure/factorisation lemma (goursat) and a combinatorial covering lemma (pfr-9-aux'). The glue is a size bound obtained by composing the two lemmas' outputs — a subspace H covered by c, factorised as H₀ × H₁.
applicability.use_when: the result is the combination of two independent, already-stated lemmas whose hypotheses line up into one chain (a covering lemma supplying H and c, a factorisation lemma supplying H₀, H₁, φ); the statement can be frozen with a Lean name and \leanok before the proof is written; and the proof is a covering-and-counting calculation over the graph of a function rather than a new construction.
applicability.avoid_when: the two lemmas' hypotheses do not line up into a single chain; a further lemma must be stated and proved (that belongs as its own node); the constants matter and any of them might change (the exponent 10 is exactly twice the covering lemma's exponent 5); or the statement may still change (then do not freeze the Lean name).

consequences: The glue's correctness rests on two hypotheses: that `pfr-9-aux'` supplies a subspace H and a covering set c with the stated bounds (A ⊆ c+H, |c| ≤ K^5 |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2}, |H|/|A| ∈ [K^{-8}, K^8]), and that `goursat` factorises H as H₀, H₁ with |H| = |H₀| |H₁|. The final estimate |c||H₁| ≤ |S|^{10} is a chain that squares the covering bound |c| ≤ |S|^5 |A|^{1/2}/|H|^{1/2} and divides by |A|, so the exponent 10 is exactly twice the exponent 5; if that constant changes, the parent's conclusion changes with it. The step 'G is covered by at most |c| translates of H₀' uses that A ⊆ c+H projects onto G as c' + H₀; it fails if the projection is not surjective. In the blueprint, `\leanok` is a claim the project's build verifies, not something the LaTeX text enforces, so a citation whose hypotheses do not line up leaves a silent gap.
